title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks sold off sharply Thursday despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO — Nasdaq -2.3%, S&P 500 -2%, Dow -1,101pts (-2.2%); the 10-year Treasury yield held above 5% (5.051%) and gold/silver hit their lowest levels in over a year (gold ~$3,628/oz) on rate-hike expectations.

Markets: Anthropic (ANT) priced its IPO at $83/share and jumped 17% in its Nasdaq debut, valuing the Claude maker at ~$1.08T (up to ~$1.5-1.8T fully diluted) in one of the largest tech listings on record; Amazon and Google will hold ~15% and ~14% nonvoting stakes, respectively.

Companies: A ransomware group leaked limited customer data from Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase; Visa fell 3% and S&P financials dropped 1.5%, while cybersecurity stocks rallied again (Palo Alto Networks +6.4%).

Companies: Williams-Sonoma led S&P decliners (-15%+) after a Pottery Barn-driven revenue slowdown tied to weak home sales; Take-Two Interactive fell 3.7% (-18% YTD) even as GTA VI launched to strong reviews.
Companies: Seven major corporations (FedEx, GE Aerospace, GM, JPMorgan, Pfizer, John Deere, United Airlines) launched an 'AI Deployer Council' to push for a bigger voice in AI regulation.

Macro/Policy: A wave of recent tech outages (Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan, United, Workday, FAA, NSA) has fueled bot-driven conspiracy theories online, with researchers finding roughly 30% of related posts came from suspected bot accounts, per Axios.

Macro/Policy: Fed officials Waller, Cook and Barkin are due to speak Friday ahead of the University of Michigan's final November consumer sentiment survey; the Fed held rates steady at 3.75-4% at its Oct. 28 meeting.
